content: QRICH1, also referred to as Glutamine-rich protein 1, is a protein in humans encoded by the QRICH1 gene. This protein is characterized by the presence of a Caspase Activation Recruitment Domain (CARD), which is a structural motif involved in various cellular processes. Due to the presence of this domain, QRICH1 is thought to play a role in pathways related to apoptosis, inflammation, and host immune responses. The QRICH1 gene spans 64,363 base pairs and encodes an mRNA transcript that is 3,331 base pairs in length. It contains 11 exons and is located on the genomic sequence between base pairs 49,057,531 and 49,141,201. The precise biological function of QRICH1 remains poorly understood. However, the CARD domain near the N-terminus of the protein suggests its involvement in apoptosis and inflammatory processes. QRICH1 is predicted to localize to the nucleus and has been shown to interact with proteins such as ATXN1 (Ataxin-1) and ATF7IP (Activating Transcription Factor 7-Interacting Protein 1). ATXN1 is implicated in RNA binding and RNA metabolism, while ATF7IP functions as a recruiter protein that links transcription factors to the general transcription machinery, influencing transcription regulation and chromatin structure. The QRICH1 protein is composed of 776 amino acids, with 109 of these being glutamine residues, accounting for 14% of the protein. It contains three distinct domains: 1. The CARD domain, which belongs to the death fold superfamily and is involved in apoptosis signaling, immune signaling, inflammation, and host defense mechanisms. 2. A glutamine-rich domain, which constitutes the majority of the protein and is highly conserved among orthologs. 3. A Domain of Unknown Function (DUF3504), located near the C-terminus of the protein sequence. All three domains are well-conserved across strict orthologs. Post-translational modifications of QRICH1 include multiple phosphorylation sites. PhosphoSitePlus has identified three phosphorylated serine residues at positions 343, 345, and 659. Additionally, the NetPhos program predicts 45 phosphorylation sites on serine, threonine, and tyrosine residues, as well as one sulfated tyrosine at position 725. No signal peptide or signal peptide cleavage sites have been predicted. QRICH1 is ubiquitously expressed throughout the human body, with particularly high expression in tissues such as the thymus, testis, cerebellar cortex, trachea, and embryonic tissues. Elevated QRICH1 expression has also been observed in certain pathological conditions, including germ cell tumors, leukemia, lymphoma, and chondrosarcoma. In terms of homology, QRICH1 is highly conserved among mammalian orthologs and other chordates, including fish, birds, and amphibians. Some conservation is observed in insects, but no orthologs have been identified in plants, fungi, or yeast. QRICH1 has five paralogs, all of which encode zinc finger proteins.
